commit.message:
Credit the lift to its authors, and fix three stale texts

Work package 17 of milestone 0.7, the remaining findings of the audit of
0.7.0rc3. Documentation and one test docstring; no code and no figure.

docs/references.md credited Prellberg with the compression and the lift.
His version 2 credits de Bondt and van den Essen with the symmetric lift,
calls the polarization subalgebra it goes through known, and claims the
collision-generated non-injective Keller subspace and the control it
gives over that lift, left unchanged. The same page says the lift is
theirs a hundred lines further down, so this is a page disagreeing with
itself and with its source at once, which is the second time in this
milestone and the second time an audit found it.

The density paragraph set his forty-variable quartic against this
project's thirty-eight and left out his thirty-eight with 340 monomials,
which the section on version 2 states correctly. Thirty-eight against
thirty-eight is the comparison and it is now the one made: 340 against
386, with the two at forty beside it, 350 against 398.

docs/contracts.md named Corollary 7's route-specific minimality for forty
in both places and not Proposition 8's for thirty-eight. Both are stated
now, each as a statement about one route, each as the paper's.

docs/api.md and one test docstring still justified a base of at least
three by the measure being zero exactly on a multi-affine map. 0.7.0rc3
removed that reason from the code and the contract page and left these
two. It holds at one and at two, where every term is positive, and fails
only at zero; the reason for three is the falling measure and nothing
else.

Two smaller ones. The entry for version 2 of arXiv:2608.12543 moves to
0.7.0rc3, where the work was done -- it was written while 0.7.0rc2 was
the open heading. And a test docstring called itself marked slow while
carrying no marker: the sentence goes rather than the marker being added,
because deselecting that test would leave the figures on three pages with
nothing checking them, and some seconds is a price worth paying for that.

None of these five was reachable by a gate. make measure checks the
figures on the references page and not the sentences around them, and no
test reads a paragraph for an attribution. Every one was found by
reading, and four of the six errata entries this milestone has are of the
same kind.

commit.message:
Rerun the exhaustiveness claims after the offer widened

Documentation only, and it belongs with work package 16 rather than
after it. Everything work packages 6 and 7 established is a negative
claim over untargeted_candidates, and WP 16 widened that offer. A
negative claim over a space that has since grown is exactly the error
the pruning rule of peel was making, so the measurements were made again
instead of assumed to carry.

Nothing moved. The candidate counts at all six maps of the published
chain are what they were, the exhaustive searches under the bound of
eleven give 2, 33, 299 and 2720 states again with no step failing the
weight rule, the reach from Alpoege's map and the rejoining table are
identical, and every row of WP 7 that was rerun -- the lever counts, the
anchor-widened searches at ten, eight and seven, and the order
measurement -- is unchanged. The five shards at n = 5 and the
anchor-widened row at n = 6 are long and are named as not rerun.

The reason it does not move is the part worth keeping. The two carrier
sets differ only on a dependency cycle, and a chain of BCWSteps does not
make one: a bought coordinate is X_u + P with P over the coordinates
already there, so the carriers a reduction produces never depend on each
other. The widening bites on a map somebody hands in and not on one this
library builds, which is why the audit's two counterexamples are both
supplied maps.

That also says what a future widening of the targeted enumerator would
have to check, and it is not the same thing: that one changes which
candidate survives deduplication, so it can remove a chain rather than
only add one.

commit.message:
Ask BCW-10 for a carried factor everywhere it is safe to

Work package 16 of milestone 0.7, the high finding of the audit of
0.7.0rc3, and the version opens 0.7.0rc4. Two of the three sites are
corrected, the third is measured and left, and no figure moves.

PolynomialMap.carrier_indices_for_factors is the shared predicate the
audit asked for: dF_j/dX_j == 1, which is BCW-10's third clause and the
whole of what a step asks of a carried slot. It always contains
carrier_indices, which asks for more because it picks out a unipotent
block: it drops every coordinate on a dependency cycle and its docstring
says it is not maximal. That is the right question for the block and the
wrong one for a factor.

untargeted._carried_values asks it now. On
(x + y^2, y + x + z, z + 2x + y^2, w + y^4) reduce_to_degree3 bought a
coordinate where one step using the first coordinate twice drops the
degree from four to three and buys nothing; it takes that step now.

peeling._stranded asks it now, and this is the release blocker rather
than a lost dimension. The rule prunes a branch standing one coordinate
above the source when the source has no carrier, since a further step
could then only buy. carrier_indices is empty on a linear map whose
coordinates depend on each other in a cycle although every one of them
satisfies BCW-10, so the premise was false: the audit found peel
reporting an exhausted space with a verified two-step chain inside its
bounds, and an exhausted space is a claim. Both maps are regression
tests.

search.anchors and enumerate_candidates still ask the narrower question,
and that is a measurement and not an oversight. Swapping the predicate in
there does not widen the space. _partner lets a carrier take a slot a
pool name would otherwise fill and found.setdefault keeps whichever came
first, so a chain the search used to find drops out: the unweighted
control of SEA-14 exhausts at 2667 states with nothing, at every budget
tried. Offering both forms is the correction, it is the same one work
package 10 made for the multi-affine walk, and it moves SEA figures, so
it is its own package. The reason sits in the code beside the line that
was not changed.

I deferred this fix twice before, in work packages 10 and 13, to keep
0.6's figures still. The price I was avoiding is zero and was measured
before this change: reduce_to_degree3 reaches the same thirteen from the
normalized Alpoege map in the same seven steps and the same map, and the
multi-affine walk reaches the same 19, 23 and 24. Deferring it let the
same conceptual error reach a place where it produced a false report.

UNT-9, UNT-12 and REV-7 say which predicate they mean. REV-7's paragraph
says why the pruning is where the narrower set stopped being a narrower
decision and became a wrong answer.
